points.reason: The synchronized TMS sample is stored from jtag_tms_i, so altered input bits can select an unintended TAP command or later block scan progress.
This wire carries the synchronized TMS value into the TAP transition tests, allowing it to select an unintended state or keep the TAP in a blocking state.
TMS controls every TAP state transition, including transitions into reset, pause, scan, and update states, so changing it can redirect or block the transport.
Changed JTAG data bits are sampled into the serial path and can later alter the operation bits or prevent a recognized operation from being issued.
The synchronized TDI bit is shifted into the DMI scan register, where altered bits can change the decoded operation or suppress a valid request.
reg_access shifts TDI into tap_reg.dmi and the DMI controller decodes its low two bits, so altered scan data can select the wrong operation or no operation.
The controller stores the recognized DMI operation in dmi_ctrl.op and only asserts busy for read or write encodings, so the selector can be changed or prevented from issuing.
The dmi_req_o.op field is driven directly from dmi_ctrl.op, so an altered or withheld selector changes or prevents the outgoing DMI operation.
The DMI controller stores, clears, and sets dmi_ctrl.err, so altering those assignments can make software receive an incorrect access-error status.
The error bit is packed into tap_reg.dmi_nxt, so changing this result-building assignment changes the reported DMI status.
reg_access captures the packed DMI result and shifts its low bits to jtag_tdo_o, so altered scan handling can misreport the error.
The controller sets and clears dmi_ctrl.busy and uses it to gate acceptance of new DMI requests, so it can be forced to block or release transactions incorrectly.
The scanned DMI word and instruction selection determine whether dmi_ctrl.busy is asserted, allowing an altered scan command to create or suppress the busy lock.
The update-valid pulse qualifies loading a DMI operation and therefore controls whether the busy lock is asserted.
